tagline: Clean the data. Preserve the meaning.
shortDescription: Data inspection, cleaning, quality auditing, transformation, joining, reshaping, validation, and reproducible data preparation.
detailedDescription: Convert messy, inconsistent, or poorly structured datasets into reliable analytical inputs without silently changing their meaning. DataMend Lab audits column schemas, flags sentinel missing values, standardizes dates and units, reshapes wide and long tables, and exports a deterministic transformation recipe alongside your cleaned dataset.
primaryPurpose: Convert messy, inconsistent, or poorly structured datasets into reliable analytical inputs without silently changing their meaning.
primaryUseCases: Diagnose messy spreadsheets, mixed data types, and sentinel missing values (e.g., -999, 'N/A')
Standardize heterogeneous timestamps into canonical ISO-8601 dates
Reshape wide report tables into tidy observation-per-row matrices
Join multi-table datasets and audit primary-key uniqueness without silent row drops
Export cleaned CSV/TSV files paired with a SHA-256 reproducible transformation log

screenshots.alt: DataMend Lab workspace showing cell-level transformation diffs, ISO-8601 date standardization, sentinel missing value recoding, and a 4-step reproducible Tidyverse/JSON pipeline.

featureHighlights: Non-destructive cell-level diff inspector
Schema & measurement-type validation (Nominal, Ordinal, Continuous, ISO-Date)
Explicit missingness auditing (zero silent row deletions)
Wide-to-long pivot reshaping & primary-key deduplication
Reproducible JSON & Tidyverse R recipe export

tagline: Understand the data. Choose the view.
brandVoice: Give your data the right perspective.
shortDescription: Data-type classification, chart recommendations, graphical construction, visual interpretation, and visualization literacy.
detailedDescription: Help users select, create, and interpret statistical visualizations grounded in perceptual psychometrics. VisualGrammar maps variable measurement types (nominal, ordinal, discrete, continuous, temporal) to the Cleveland–McGill hierarchy of elementary perceptual tasks, compares alternative chart families side-by-side through Known Visualization Unity, and runs a 15-point pre-flight perceptual and accessibility audit.
primaryPurpose: Help users select, create, and interpret statistical visualizations.
primaryUseCases: Classify dataset variables and discover perceptually accurate chart encodings
Compare how histograms, KDEs, boxplots, violin plots, and beeswarms represent the same data
Audit charts for mathematical Lie Factor (0.95 to 1.05), zero-baseline rules, and direct labeling
Construct OKLCH perceptually uniform, deuteranopia/protanopia-safe palettes
Export declarative Vega-Lite specifications, publication SVGs, and ggplot2 code

screenshots.alt: VisualGrammar workspace demonstrating Known Visualization Unity across three cohorts with identical group means (50.0) but distinct unimodal, bimodal, and skewed distributions alongside a 15-point perceptual audit.

featureHighlights: Cleveland–McGill perceptual channel ranking engine
Known Visualization Unity side-by-side chart family comparator
15-point pre-flight Lie Factor & zero-baseline auditor
OKLCH perceptually uniform & colorblind-safe palette studio
Vega-Lite JSON, crisp SVG, and R ggplot2 code export

showcaseTheme: The numbers don't tell the whole story.
shortDescription: Interactive bivariate dataset synthesis, exact-moment control, correlation, regression, residual analysis, and diagnostic exploration.
detailedDescription: Reveal how datasets with identical summary statistics (means, standard deviations, correlation r, and OLS regression lines) can conceal radically different geometric structures, curvature, and high-leverage anomalies. QuartetLab pairs an interactive bivariate canvas and Gram-Schmidt exact-moment solver with synchronized Residual vs. Fitted and Normal Q-Q plots, live Cook's distance halos, and Minitab/R-standard regression output.
primaryPurpose: Reveal how datasets with similar statistical summaries can behave very differently.
primaryUseCases: Drag observations in real time while locking exact sample moments (x̄, s_x, ȳ, s_y, r, R²)
Investigate Anscombe's Quartet, non-linear curvature traps, and high-leverage outliers
Inspect synchronized Residuals vs. Fitted (e_i vs. ŷ_i) and Normal Q-Q diagnostic canvases
Audit point-by-point leverage (h_i), standardized residuals, and Cook's distance (D_i > 4/n)
Export datasets and Minitab/R regression tables to CSV, R, Python, LaTeX, TI-84, or printable FRQ worksheets

screenshots.alt: QuartetLab dual-canvas workbench showing Anscombe III bivariate scatterplot with OLS line, Cook's distance vermilion halo on Observation #3, synchronized Residuals vs Fitted and Normal Q-Q plots, and Minitab/R regression output table.

featureHighlights: Live Gram-Schmidt exact-moment lock solver
Synchronized Scatter, Residual (e_i vs. ŷ_i), and Normal Q-Q canvases
Cook's distance (D_i > 4/n) and high-leverage (h_i > 4/n) visual halos
Minitab / R / AP-standard regression computer output table
One-click export to CSV, R, Python, TI-84 lists, LaTeX, and FRQ PDF worksheets

shortDescription: Probability, sampling, bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation testing, computational inference, and simulation.
detailedDescription: Help users understand randomness, quantify uncertainty, and investigate statistical evidence through direct computational experiments. ResampleLab makes the distinction between raw sample data, bootstrap resampling with replacement (for confidence intervals and standard errors), and null-model permutation shuffling (for exact and randomization p-values) visually concrete and reproducible via seeded PRNGs.
primaryPurpose: Help users understand randomness, quantify uncertainty, and investigate statistical evidence.
primaryUseCases: Construct nonparametric percentile, studentized-t, and bootstrap confidence intervals
Run one-sample, two-sample, matched-pairs, and regression permutation hypothesis tests
Compare empirical bootstrap distributions against classical normal and Student-t approximations
Explore Central Limit Theorem convergence and sampling variability across sample sizes
Export reproducible simulation summaries, seeded draw logs, and R/Python resampling scripts

screenshots.alt: ResampleLab workspace displaying a 10,000-replicate bootstrap distribution for a skewed sample median, highlighting the 95% percentile confidence interval [39.15, 46.72], vermilion 2.5% tails, and method comparison table.

featureHighlights: Deterministic seeded PRNG for 100% reproducible simulations
Side-by-side Bootstrap (with replacement) vs. Permutation (null shuffle) engines
Live comparison of Percentile, Studentized-t*, and Classical intervals
Interactive step-by-step single-draw and 10,000-draw batch visualizer
Explicit scope guardrails distinguishing sampling error from selection bias

tagline: Understand patterns. Forecast what comes next.
shortDescription: Time-series exploration, decomposition, forecasting methods, temporal cross-validation, uncertainty, and model diagnostics.
detailedDescription: Make statistically responsible forecasts and understand their reliability. ForecastLab implements the complete tidy forecasting workflow: chronological indexing, STL trend-seasonality-remainder decomposition, benchmark baselines (Naïve, Seasonal Naïve, Drift), ETS state-space and SARIMA modeling, rolling-origin temporal cross-validation, innovation residual autocorrelation diagnostics, and calibrated 80%/95% prediction interval fan charts.
primaryPurpose: Make statistically responsible forecasts and understand their reliability.
primaryUseCases: Decompose time series into Trend (T_t), Seasonal (S_t), and Remainder (R_t) components via STL
Compare ETS state-space and SARIMA models against Seasonal Naïve and Drift benchmarks
Evaluate out-of-sample accuracy across rolling forecast origins using MASE, RMSE, and MAE
Inspect innovation residual ACF/PACF correlograms and Ljung-Box white-noise diagnostics
Communicate future uncertainty honestly with 80% and 95% prediction interval fan charts

screenshots.alt: ForecastLab workspace showing historical monthly series, forecast origin divider, ETS damped trend point predictions with 80% and 95% prediction interval fans, STL decomposition panels, MASE accuracy leaderboard, and residual ACF plot.

featureHighlights: STL additive & Box-Cox transformed seasonal decomposition
Mandatory benchmark comparison (Seasonal Naïve, Drift, Mean)
Chronological train/test holdout & rolling-origin cross-validation
Innovation residual ACF/PACF and Ljung-Box portmanteau diagnostics
Calibrated 80% and 95% prediction interval ribbons & R fable/feasts export
supportedInputs: Bundled macro, energy, and ecological time series
typicalOutputs: Forecast horizon table with 80%/95% prediction intervals (CSV)
